text:
Thomas Harley plays almost 25 minutes a night for Dallas, and over the last ten games that has climbed toward 26. He is the defenseman the Stars lean on, and the 5v5 numbers back the trust: 54% of shot attempts and 53% of expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, nearly four points better than the team without him.

The production is fine rather than loud, 11 points in 17 games with five on the power play. His three-point night against San Jose on Nov. 7 got him headlines, and so did the trade speculation, though that is chatter, not reporting of anything real.

The question mark is defense. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, with opponents getting more chances when he was out there (bottom 10% of defensemen). This year's shot share is a better look. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows a defenseman who joins the rush more than most (28% of his shots, typical is 17%), which is the part of his game to watch.
headline: Harley carries Dallas minutes, not yet the scoreboard
